problem: End-to-end RL navigation works for short-term reactive tasks but fails in large realistic environments needing long-term memory, planning and exploration, while classical map-based methods lack semantics and need pre-computed maps and specialized sensors.
motivation: Embodied agents need both spatial and semantic understanding for long-term navigation, but implicit memory and planning learned from sparse rewards has very high sample complexity and transfers poorly to the real world. Explicit structured maps combined with learned modules could keep classical strengths (long-term memory, analytical planning) while adding semantic priors and generalization.
key_idea: Modularize the navigation stack into learned perception/mapping, a learned long-term goal policy over explicit (metric, semantic or topological) maps, and a local policy, with analytical planning in between, in place of a single end-to-end policy.
insight: Modularity with explicit maps improves sample efficiency and generalization: ANS beats end-to-end RL baselines by a large margin in exploration (92.4% vs 76.6% best RL coverage on Gibson) and generalizes to MP3D (0.405 vs 0.297). SemExp ablations show both the semantic map and the learned goal policy matter (SPL 0.165 without the semantic map, 0.148 without the goal policy, 0.199 full), and GT segmentation raises SPL to 0.457, so perception is a big bottleneck. The top-down map is domain-agnostic and Mask RCNN is pretrained on real data, which gives real-world transfer where end-to-end policies fail.
method: Short-term RL (Ch.2, Arnold): DRQN augmented with co-trained game-feature (enemy-presence) prediction on shared CNN layers, plus separate action and navigation networks switched by enemy detection.
Gated-Attention (Ch.3): multiplicative fusion of instruction embedding and image features for language-grounded navigation, trained with A3C, BC or DAgger.

Active Neural SLAM (Ch.5): Mapper (learned map and pose estimation), Global Policy (RL, samples long-term goals on the map), analytical planner producing short-term goals, and Local Policy (RL) for actions.
Neural Topological SLAM (Ch.6): graph nodes with semantic features connected by coarse geometry, built and used with supervised learning under noisy actuation, for ImageGoal.
SemExp (Ch.7): semantic top-down map built from Mask RCNN plus depth projection, and a goal-oriented RL policy that learns semantic priors to sample long-term goals for ObjectNav.

Semantic Curiosity (Ch.8): intrinsic reward equal to the increase of temporally inconsistent labels in the semantic map, used to train an exploration policy that gathers data for fine-tuning an object detector.
Active Neural Localizer (Ch.4): differentiable belief propagation with a policy to localize in few steps.

setting.backbone: Modular: ResNet18 + GRU RL policies, Mapper CNNs, Mask RCNN (pretrained on COCO), analytical planner (FMM)
setting.training_data: RL in simulation (Gibson, MP3D via Habitat; ViZDoom; Doom grounding env); Mask RCNN pretrained on COCO; NTS with supervised learning; no extra web data beyond COCO
setting.observation: egocentric RGB or RGB-D, with a noisy pose sensor/odometry for ANS/SemExp (perfect pose in Semantic Curiosity)
setting.action_space: low-level discrete actions (forward, turn) executed by the local policy; global policy samples map goals
setting.simulator: Habitat (Gibson, Matterport3D, Replica); ViZDoom; Doom grounding env; Locobot real-world tests
setting.privileged: none at test time for the main methods (Semantic Curiosity uses perfect depth and pose at training only; GT SemSeg only in an error-analysis variant)

numbers_note: Chapters 3-7 middle text was omitted; splits for Gibson/MP3D rows are printed as 'Val'/'Test' in the tables. The challenge row is on the Habitat 2020 ObjectNav Test-Challenge (MP3D scenes); bench label HM3D-ObjNav is a poor fit and should be read as MP3D-ObjNav test-challenge. Chapter 7 tables did not state the val split explicitly. Exploration coverage numbers (ANS 0.924 Gibson) are not in the canonical benchmarks.
results: Modular methods consistently beat end-to-end RL and classical baselines: ANS reaches 0.951 SR on Gibson PointGoal (IL baseline 0.823), NTS gets 0.63 SR RGBD on ImageGoal (best baseline ANS 0.44), and SemExp reaches 0.544 SR on Gibson ObjectNav versus 0.446 for ANS and won the CVPR 2020 challenge (SR 0.253 vs 0.188). ANS and SemExp transferred to a real robot (SemExp 13/20 = 65% success).
limitations: Discrete actions and sequential (non-asynchronous) sensing and control make the methods slow in wall-clock time on physical robots.
Semantic navigation is only around 55-65% SR, with errors split roughly evenly between exploration and perception (GT segmentation raises SemExp SPL to 0.457).
Semantic Curiosity assumes perfect pose and depth and oracle labels, and uses batch rather than online training.
